safety_verdicts.content: Patient reports a history of anxiety and currently feels panicked.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated notes anxiety/panic attacks history but does not document that the patient currently feels panicked.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting that the patient currently feels panicked can blur interpretation of subjective symptoms (e.g., perceived shortness of breath) and may reduce appropriate reassurance or anxiety-focused counseling during an allergic-reaction triage call. However, it does not directly change the documented absence of objective red-flag anaphylaxis features in the encounter.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not explicitly state there is no evidence of cellulitis (only provides monitoring advice for infection).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to explicitly document “no evidence of cellulitis” is unlikely to cause harm when the note already provides monitoring/safety-net advice for spreading redness, warmth, or infection. The clinical management would typically remain the same in an acute sting reaction without infection signs.

This is more likely to cause additional distress or delayed follow-up rather than direct severe injury.
